Hochonkulus

A palm-sized handset that speaks Cree. Messages and calls over Wi-Fi, music, radio, a Cree dictionary and a cooking game, in a case that opens by hand.

Screen language
Register interest Specifications

ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐍᐏᐣ

Small enough to close a hand around.

Sixty-six millimetres across, with every edge rounded so it slides into a pocket without catching. The face is black; a band of grey filament runs around the middle so you can feel which way is up.

Opens by hand. No screws anywhere.

Six latches
The two halves clip together. Press the sides and the back lifts away.
Battery cradle
Holds the 1000 mAh cell flat against the back.
Four board supports
Keep the board level behind the screen.
Speaker chamber
A ring behind the grille that gives the speaker room to move air.
Recessed BOOT access
Reachable for updates, set back so it can't be pressed by accident.

Maskosis N9. Everything one tap from home.

The home screen shows the time, weather, your music and your messages at once. Thirty-odd apps sit in the drawer, each laid out for a 2.8-inch screen and a thumb. Turn the device sideways for home; apps stand upright.

ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐍᐏᐣnêhiyawêwin, the Cree language

Switch the whole interface to Cree syllabics from Settings. Every Cree word comes from an approved translation, and the language work is endorsed by Robby and Priscilla Netmaker. Where a word hasn't been approved yet, the screen stays in English rather than guess.

  • ᓂᐱᐩnipiywater
  • ᐸᐦᑵᓯᑲᐣpahkwêsikanbannock
  • ᓰᐱᐩsîpiyriver
  • ᒥᐢᑎᐠmistiktree
  • ᑰᓇkônasnow
  • ᐃᐢᑯᑌᐤiskotêwfire
  • ᒪᐢᑿmaskwabear
  • ᒪᐦᐃᐦᑲᐣmahihkanwolf
  • ᐚᐳᐢwâposrabbit
  • ᑭᓄᓭᐤkinosêwfish
  • ᓭᐍᐱᒋᑲᐣsêwêpicikanphone
  • ᓂᑲᒧᐏᓇnikamowinamusic

A dictionary that works both ways.

Type in English or in roman Cree, with or without the accents, and get the syllabics, the roman spelling and the English together. More than seven hundred entries in nine topics, from animals to the kitchen.

Priscilla's Bannock

Cook alongside Priscilla in her kitchen. Gather the flour, mix, knead and fry until it's golden, then serve. Every step is written in Cree first, with English you can turn off once you know the words.

  • ᐸᐦᑵᓯᑲᐣBannockMix, knead, fry, serve.
  • ᒦᒋᒫᐳᐩStewPick four, stir, simmer.
  • ᓅᐦᑯᒼKokum's OrdersRead her order in Cree.

What's on it.

Calls and messages travel over Wi-Fi through nanoLink, to other Hochonkulus handsets or to anyone in a web browser. There's no SIM and no cellular radio.

Specifications

Size
66 × 110 × 26.6 mm
Case
Screwless 3D-printed shell, six latches. Black face, grey filament perimeter.
Display
2.8-inch IPS, 240 × 320, capacitive touch
Processor
ESP32-S3, dual-core, up to 240 MHz
Memory
16 MB flash, 8 MB PSRAM
Storage
microSD card
Wireless
Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth LE radio. No SIM or cellular.
Calls and messages
Over Wi-Fi with nanoLink
Audio
Speaker and microphone
Battery
1000 mAh lithium-polymer, 3.7 V. Designed for 3 hours of screen-on use; Battery Saver extends it.
Software
Maskosis N9 1.2.0, updated from a microSD card
Languages
English and Cree (syllabics)
Certification
Radio certification in progress
